column3: “Answered and said” is rendered “responded.”
The Hebrew “will you make ends of words” is rendered “will you hunt for words”; the meaning is uncertain. “Consider” is rendered “Show understanding.”
“Cattle” is rendered “beasts.”
The Hebrew has “his” self and anger; NASB has “yourself” and “your anger.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“The steps of his vigor are restricted” is rendered “His vigorous stride is shortened.”
“Caught” is rendered “thrown,” and “network” as “webbing.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Rope” is rendered “noose.”
“Scatter him to his feet” is rendered “harry him at every step.”
“His trouble is hungry” is rendered “His strength is famished,” and “for his stumbling” as “at his side.” The meaning is uncertain.
The Hebrew repeats “it consumes the parts of his skin”; NASB has “His skin is devoured by disease.”
“His trust” is rendered “the security of”; “it makes him march” is rendered “they march him.”
“Because not belonging to him” is rendered “nothing of his”; the meaning is uncertain. “Sulfur” is rendered “Brimstone.”
“Withers” is rendered “is cut off.”
“On the face of the street” is rendered “abroad.”
“People drive him” is rendered “He is driven.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Those behind and those before” is rendered “Those in the west … those in the east”; it may also mean later and earlier generations. NASB supplies “fate.”
Close to the Hebrew.
